description: This database is the most complete census of American hospitals: for every responding hospital it records how many beds of each kind it has, which services and facilities it offers, how many admissions, births, operations and emergency visits it handles, and how it is staffed and organised. It is produced by the American Hospital Association, which has run its Annual Survey of hospitals since 1946. Coverage is more than 6,200 hospitals and 400 health systems in the United States, with electronic files from 1980 onwards. Each record carries over 1,300 data points on location and ownership, system affiliation, bed counts including emergency department beds, service lines, utilisation, workforce, physician arrangements, finances, telehealth and technology adoption. The data are available only under a paid licence through AHA Data, with a download for licensed users, so it is not free; the survey questionnaire is published openly. Caveats: some items are imputed for non-respondents, licence terms restrict redistribution, and definitions change between survey years. Simulation uses: building the national inventory of hospital capacity and services for surge, evacuation and network access models. Related records: the CMS hospital provider data (data-cms-provider-data-hospitals) and HCRIS cost reports (data-cms-hcris-cost-reports) are free alternatives covering Medicare-certified hospitals.
